definition: Correlation is the relationship or association between two measured factors, such as personality traits and perceived stress. In mental health research, it describes that variables vary together, without by itself showing that one causes the other.

reasons: The packet shows correlation used as a relationship between selected personality traits and perceived stress, but it does not support the broader dictionary-style definition that correlation is generally an association between any two measured factors.
The statement that correlation means variables vary together and does not by itself show causation is not stated in the packet and goes beyond the supplied source.

The packet supports only that the study assesses a “correlation between selected personality traits and the level of perceived stress.” It does not provide a general definition of correlation as a relationship between two measured factors.
The definition’s wording that “variables vary together” is not stated or supported in the packet.
The definition’s claim that correlation “by itself show[s] that one causes the other” (i.e., does not establish causation) is not mentioned or supported in the packet.
